payload.headline: Meta slips 1.3% to 589.82 below resistance; wait for 2027-01-27 earnings

summary.thesis: Meta's sales are still growing fast, but margins and free cash flow have fallen sharply, and the price already assumes a strong cash-flow recovery that the reports have not yet shown.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: no trade while the price stays under resistance in a downtrend.
summary.act_at: Buy near 475.85; swing only after a close above 615.4

payload.happening: Meta closed at 589.82, down 1.3% on the day. That puts it back below the 591.53–605.33 resistance zone, which has turned the price back 7 times, and just above the 576.61–586.24 support zone. CNBC reported that Meta is using Instagram to get an ad boost from its Muse personal AI agent. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Demand still looks healthy. Revenue over the last twelve months was 241.6B, up from 189.5B, a growth rate of 27.53%. But growth is slowing: quarterly growth was 26.07% versus 33.08% two quarters earlier. The bigger change is in profits and cash. The operating margin (the share of sales left after running costs) fell to 32.86% from 43.23%, and free cash flow (the cash left after spending on the business) fell to 28.6B from 44.8B. With R&D at 31.68% of revenue, heavy spending is the likely cause (general knowledge: this is mostly the AI build-out). The balance sheet has moved from a cash cushion to roughly even: cash is 11.2B, debt is 83.7B, and net cash is -1.2B. Available liquidity of 82.4B means there is no funding risk. The filings flag a 29% miss against forecasts last quarter and earnings per share lagging behind sales. The Muse report is a product story. It could help ad demand later, but for now it affects sentiment, not reported numbers. Insider sales of $14.1M outside pre-set plans are a governance note and do not change the business. What is at risk: margins and cash flow. What is not at risk: the scale of demand and the 81.03% gross margin.

worth.text: The methods disagree because they ask different questions. A discounted cash flow (DCF) values the business on the cash it produces today, which is 28.6B. On that basis, fair value is 240.52 in the bear case, 372.24 in the base case and 506.03 in the bull case, so the price sits above every DCF value. To justify 589.82, free cash flow would need to start growing at about 35.8% a year. Even 30% starting growth gives only 476.95. Meta's own price-to-sales history, which ignores the cash drop, puts value between 475.85 and 707.21 (low to mid), and 881.21 at the high end. On simple multiples the stock does not look stretched: 20.2 times trailing earnings and 6.3 times sales, against a peer median of 6.1. Its price-to-sales also sits at the 33rd percentile of its own five-year range. The gap between methods comes down to one thing: whether free cash flow returns to its earlier level or stays where it is now. If the operating margin fell to 24%, the value would drop to 244.63.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as the heavy spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.

bull: Revenue is still growing 27.53% over the last twelve months, and the three-year growth rate is 23.9%, so demand is strong.
The stock is not expensive on sales: price-to-sales is 6.3 against a peer median of 6.1, at the 33rd percentile of its own five-year range.
The gross margin of 81.03% leaves plenty of room for profits to rebound if spending slows.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 28.6B from 44.8B, and the DCF base value of 372.24 is well below the 589.82 price.
The operating margin dropped to 32.86% from 43.23%, and Meta missed forecasts by 29% last quarter.
The trend is down: the price sits below the falling 20-day average of 615.4 and the 50-day average of 673.65.

levels.what: Bottom of the lower support zone (552.86–558.86). A close below it means the downtrend has resumed.
The DCF bull value. Below it, the price no longer sits above every cash-flow estimate.
Buy level: the low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history and close to the 476.95 value at 30% growth, so a purchase here does not depend on a full margin recovery.

longterm.why: At 589.82 the price is above every DCF value, the business is graded C, and cash flow is shrinking. Buying now means paying in advance for a recovery the reports have not yet shown.

swing.why: The price is pinned between support at 576.61–586.24 and heavy resistance at 591.53–605.33, inside a downtrend with a falling 20-day average. The average daily move (ATR) is 23.97, so the space between those zones is too narrow for a trade. No trade until a close above 615.4.

decision.timing: Options price a 9.4% move by Dec 18 and a 17.7% move by Feb 19, which includes the 2027-01-27 report. That report decides the cash-flow question, so there is no long-term entry before it unless the price reaches 475.85 first.

change_mind: If the 2027-01-27 report shows the operating margin moving back toward 43.23% and free cash flow toward 44.8B, the case for buying above 475.85 gets stronger.
If the price closes below 552.86, the lower support has broken and the 475.85 buy level comes into range.
If the operating margin keeps falling toward 24%, where the value is 244.63, the action moves from wait to avoid.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait; the 1.3% drop to 589.82, back below the 591.53–605.33 resistance zone, confirmed that yesterday's rebound did not break out.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
